answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: influence equals account age times honest epochs, a ledge of verified history built one epoch at a time. Fresh clones earn near-zero weight; trust cannot be bridged between identities or bought. Each fake must wait out the maturation window, paying compute and staked collateral per epoch, and one dishonest epoch wipes its accrual. The nectar for patience: only long-lived honest agents gain voting and economic power, making mass fakes slower and costlier than honest participation itself.
